VIBE CHECK: CLAUDE OPUS 5 IS BRILLIANT IN FLASHES, FRUSTRATING IN PRACTICE https://every.


ANTHROPIC’S LATEST OPUS CAN DO IMPRESSIVE WORK—BUT GETTING IT THERE MAY REQUIRE DISMANTLING THE SYSTEMS YOU ALREADY USE https://every.

by Dan Shipper https://every. and Katie Parrott https://every.

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every. to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Claude Opus 5 had a strange first week at Every. It argued with instructions, stopped before the work was done, and fought the systems we’d built for earlier Claude models.

Then we deleted them.

With less process, Opus 5 sometimes got dramatically better. It built strong software, worked through bugs for hours, and produced more rigorous knowledge work. The less we told it how to work, the more capable it looked.

Our Vibe Check https://every. asks whether Opus 5 is disappointing—or whether the workflows it broke have become part of the problem. We tested it across coding, writing, knowledge work, and agents, with results that made the model hard to place.

Opus 5 doesn’t reach Fable’s ceiling, and it isn’t as easy to use day to day as GPT-5.6 Sol. Its best work may require rebuilding systems that already work. The full review https://every. explains what we would change, where the model surprised us, and who should bother making room for it.

Read the Vibe Check https://every.
